title: Sin excludes from favor and binds under just penalty—debtor before God
source_text: I. Peccatum cum sit aliquid Dei naturae & legibus adversum, & quo summa Dei Majestas offenditur, hominem Dei favore & gratia excludit, eumque reddit obnoxium poenis, quibus divina justitia postulat talem offensam vindicari, earumque debitorem apud Deum illum constituit.
pass_a_gloss: Sin, being something adverse to the nature and laws of God, and by which the supreme Majesty of God is offended, excludes a man from the favor and grace of God, and renders him liable to the penalties by which divine justice demands that such an offense be vindicated, and constitutes him a debtor for those penalties before God.
pass_b_english: Sin against God’s nature and law offends infinite Majesty and shuts a man out of favor.
Justice then holds him debtor to the penalties that such offense requires.

choices.why: Remission will mean release from this debt-relation.
